text: One evening when everyone was going to bed at Mosfell, Egil called in two of Grims slaves. He told them to fetch him a horse, because I want to go to bathe in the pool. When he was ready he went out, taking his chests of silver with him. He mounted the horse, crossed the hayfields to the slope that begins there and disappeared. In the morning, when all the people got up, they saw Egil wandering around on the hill east of the farm, leading a horse behind him. They went over to him and brought him home. But neither the slaves nor the chests of treasure ever returned, and there are many theories about where Egil hid his treasure. East of the farm is a gully leading down from the mountain. It has been noticed that English coins have been found in the gully when the river recedes after floods caused by sudden thaws. Some people believe Egil must have hidden his treasure there. Then there are large and exceptionally deep marshes below the hayfields at Mosfell, and it is claimed that Egil threw his treasure into them. On the south side of the rivers are hot springs with big pits nearby, where some people believe Egil must have hidden his treasure, because a will-o-the-wisp is often seen there. Egil himself said he had killed Grims slaves and hidden his treasure somewhere, but he never told a single person where it was. Egils Saga (trans. Bernard Scudder 1997)
